reason: Attacked on the one axis that could kill it, translation drift, and it survives. Anne Frank's diary exists in English in two incompatible renderings and the older one would have been an easy mistake: Barbara Mooyaart-Doubleday's 1952 text gives this sentence as give pleasure to the people around me who yet don't know me, which is a different sentence about a different circle of people. The proposed wording, to be useful or bring enjoyment to all people, even those I've never met, is the wording of the 1995 Definitive Edition in Susan Massotty's translation, and Open Library's search inside returns that exact string from scans of The Diary of a Young Girl itself and from Mirjam Pressler's Anne Frank: A Hidden Life, Pressler being the co-editor of the Definitive Edition, which is as close to an in-house witness as a secondary book gets. Note one near miss the editor should not confuse for a hit: the top result is Goodrich and Hackett's stage play The Diary of Anne Frank, which prints useful AND bring enjoyment. The proposal has the OR, which is the diary's. Locator: Wikiquote's Anne Frank page, which cites entries by date, puts both this sentence and I want to go on living even after my death under 5 April 1944, and puts them in that order, with I don't want to have lived in vain like most people immediately before, so the verifier's locator (near the close of the 5 April 1944 entry, just before I want to go on living even after my death) is right in both the date and the position. Attribution: the diary is hers, the misattribution list does not touch her, and nothing here is a floating internet slogan. Scope: first published 1947, translated 1995, both well before 1999; a diary, not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory; and it is the hopeful sentence of that entry rather than anything needing a warning, so it reads at six in the morning. Theme: usefulness to people one has never met is exactly September's debt to other people. Tag Diary is the form of the work, and unlike the Merton in this same batch it is a real dated entry. Form: the source line leads with her name, carries no dash and no straight double quote, ends in a full stop, and runs 118 characters against the 140 cap; it names the translator and the year of the translation whose wording it uses, as rule 4 requires. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, not banned, anne frank at 2 of 3 from months 1 and 7. ONE CAUTION, not a refutation: this is her THIRD and last line of the year. If the editor has a stronger Frank line held for a later month, this spends the slot.
